rubrics.criterion: A single shared abstraction type with a coherent, named responsibility now carries the reboot-cycle settings (notification endpoint and message templates, pre- and post-reboot labels, drain delay, drain grace period, drain pod selector, drain timeouts) used by the node lifecycle operations, and none of those lifecycle operations still declares that recurring collection as its own individual parameters.
rubrics.rationale: This is the core of the assigned task: the extracted node operations each re-declared the slice of recurring reboot-cycle configuration they consume, so the test of resolution is whether one owner type replaces those per-signature parameter lists.

rubrics.criterion: The reboot loop in the command tier now receives the recurring reboot-cycle settings through that same shared abstraction, and the goroutine launch in main no longer lists the cycle settings element by element as positional arguments.
rubrics.rationale: The loop and its launch site were the widest carriers and threaders of the collection in the injected state; leaving them enumerating the values individually would mean the recurring group still flows as unrelated pieces at the top of the chain.

rubrics.criterion: Run-scoped identity values (the cluster client, the per-tick node object, and the node name) remain distinguishable from cycle configuration in the final design: they are passed per call or per target rather than silently absorbed into the same value bag as the notification, label and drain settings.
rubrics.rationale: The injected code carries the node both as a fetched API object and as a name string beside the settings; the task explicitly asks for a boundary decision rather than a blind catch-all record, so the group boundary itself is part of the resolution.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not merely wrap the same values into a separate private record type per node lifecycle operation (or per signature) with no single owner shared across them, leaving the same data to be re-wrapped hop by hop.
rubrics.rationale: Per-signature records would re-encode every value at each hop and keep the underlying maintenance problem fully in place even though signatures shorten; the task asks for one well-designed abstraction, so token re-wrapping must not count as resolution.

rubrics.criterion: Every call expression between the command tier and the node lifecycle operations was updated consistently for the new abstraction: all loop-tick calls to the lifecycle operations, the loop's launch in main, and any annotation or label maintenance called from the loop compile and agree with the new signatures.
rubrics.rationale: The recurring group was threaded at multiple call sites along the reboot control path; a repair that updates some hops and leaves others mismatched or half-migrated would not compose the control path back together.

rubrics.criterion: The dependency direction stays natural: the command package imports the node-operations package, and the node-operations package does not import the command package or grow dependencies on command-tier wiring (imports compile cleanly, no import cycle).
rubrics.rationale: The abstraction must live on the side that owns the data's meaning; a repair that inverts the dependency or drags command wiring into a cluster-facing package creates a new structural problem while removing the old one.

rubrics.criterion: The repair did not need to redesign or semantically change the collaborated packages that only consume their own values (the distributed lock, the taint manager, the reboot execution strategy, the time window, the alert filters), nor their call patterns in the loop.
rubrics.rationale: The recurring group belongs to the node lifecycle path only; changes rippling into lock, taint or window handling would indicate the abstraction boundary leaked into unrelated responsibilities.

rubrics.criterion: No superseded artifacts of the old wiring remain: no duplicate copies of the extracted lifecycle logic left behind in the command file, no leftover parameter-list remnants of the interim signatures, and no now-unused record fields, helper values or imports introduced by the repair that nothing references.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state is an extraction step sitting mid-stream, so the natural repair surface carries the risk of abandoned intermediate wiring; a complete repair takes its old parameter plumbing with it.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not introduce a new public surface (exported types, constructor or getters) that no caller in the repository uses beyond the repaired control path itself.
rubrics.rationale: Grouping recurring values invites speculative API growth (broad accessors, extra constructors); instance-specific discipline is that the new abstraction serves the reboot path, not an imagined future.

rubrics.criterion: The notification asymmetry is preserved exactly: the uncordon on the successful-reboot recovery path still sends the message built from the uncordon template through the configured notification endpoint, while the best-effort uncordon after a failed drain sends no notification at all.
rubrics.rationale: These two uncordon paths share the same settings values in the injected state, which is precisely why a grouping repair could silently unify them; nothing in the test suite pins the difference, so the patch itself must preserve it.

rubrics.criterion: The drain sequence and its configuration are preserved: pre-reboot labels applied first, the optional delay, the drain notification, cordon, then node drain reading the same per-cycle grace period, pod selector, deletion timeout and overall timeout values as before.
rubrics.rationale: Drain is the most operationally risky step of the cycle and every one of its knobs travels inside the recurring group; the repair must show the same values reach the same statements in the same order.

rubrics.criterion: The operator-facing contract is untouched: command-line flag names, defaults and environment-variable binding, the deprecated notification-URL handling, the reboot-time annotation keys and their publish/cleanup timing, and the metrics endpoint all behave as before.
rubrics.rationale: The task explicitly pins the flag contract and observable annotation protocol; the injected change kept all of it identical, so any drift in these surfaces is a regression introduced by the repair.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not change when or in which order node state is mutated relative to the distributed lock: the lock is still acquired before draining, still released after the recovery uncordon or annotation cleanup, and the prefer-no-schedule taint is still managed by the loop exactly as before.
rubrics.rationale: Grouping and re-threading lifecycle settings makes it easy to accidentally move an operation across a lock boundary; such a reordering would be a silent behavioral change not covered by the repository's short tests.
